Article Title: How ABVP retained Panjab University presidency with just one more vote than last year
Article Text:
Jubilant ABVP candidates and their supporters celebrate their win





CHANDIGARH: The Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad’s ( ABVP ) second successive presidential victory at Panjab University was shaped by a combination of organisational unity, the return of last year’s breakaway faction to the campaign fold, influence of large voting departments and a divided field of rivals.ABVP’s Ankit secured 3,149 votes, defeating ASAP’s (Association of Students for Alternative Politics) Aadil Brar, who polled 2,637. NSUI ’s (National Students’ Union of India) Gurman Singh Sidhu secured 2,263 votes, while SATH’s Darshpreet Singh got 1,387.ASAP entered the contest with considerable political firepower, with AAP MP Meet Hayer and MLA Amritpal Singh Sukhanand handling its campaign. NSUI, meanwhile, received public backing from senior Congress leaders, including Punjab Congress chief Amarinder Singh Raja Warring and Himachal Pradesh chief minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu.ABVP’s advantage was continuity. It had an organisation that had already won the presidency, a campaign team with experience and a candidate who was not new to campus politics.Among the four presidential candidates, Ankit was the only contender apart from Darshpreet to have been visible in PU politics for several years. Aadil Brar, though a relatively fresh presidential face, had served as UILS department representative and had an established campus network.Gurman was the freshest of the principal contenders — a disadvantage in an election where name recognition, personal networks and mobilisation can matter as much as party labels.The biggest change, however, came within ABVP itself. Last year, the breakaway ABVP Front had contested separately, with its candidate Naveen Kumar finishing second in the vice-president race with 2,828 votes. This time, several of those who had emerged as potential kingmakers were back in the ABVP campaign.Former PU ABVP campus president Rajat Puri, Political Science research scholar Vishal Malik, former UILS student Saksham Sharma and outgoing PUCSC president Gaurav Veer Sohal were actively involved. North Zone organising secretary Gaurav Attri, under whose organisational charge ABVP won its first PU presidency last year, was again involved.Significantly, ABVP did not need to increase its presidential vote. Ankit’s 3,149 votes were just one more than Sohal’s 3,148 last year. The total presidential votes, including NOTA, were also almost unchanged — 9,610 this year against 9,613 last year.What changed was the configuration around that vote. Last year’s eight-cornered contest allowed multiple candidates to occupy different pockets of the anti-ABVP vote. This year, the field was reduced to four, concentrating the contest but leaving the opposition split among ASAP, NSUI and SATH. ABVP was therefore able to retain roughly one-third of the presidential vote.
Article Summary: The Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad’s ( ABVP ) second successive presidential victory at Panjab University was shaped by a combination of organisational unity, the return of last year's breakaway faction to the campaign fold, influence of large voting departments and a divided field of rivals. The biggest change, however, came within ABVP itself.

Article Title: Amid row, Chhattisgarh judge named as Rajasthan HC Chief Justice
Article Text:
The Supreme Court Collegium recommended Justice Sanjay K Agarwal as Chief Justice for Rajasthan High Court.





JAIPUR: The Supreme Court Collegium recommended Justice Sanjay K Agarwal of Chhattisgarh HC as Chief Justice of Rajasthan HC late Monday, ending a nearly yearlong stint under acting CJ Sanjeev Prakash Sharma as protests by lawyers over his functioning intensified. The Collegium also recommended Justice Pushpendra Singh Bhati as CJ of J&K HC.Hours before the recommendation, Sharma decided to abstain from judicial work from Sept 1 to 5. Rajasthan HC administration issued an amended roster for the period, assigning PIL matters to court no. 3, comprising Justice Inderjeet Singh and Justice Sandeep Taneja.The move came as two Jodhpur bar associations extended their boycott of Justice Sharma till Sept 6, demanding he be kept away from judicial and administrative duties. Rajasthan HC Lawyers’ Association and Rajasthan HC Advocates’ Association of Jodhpur resolved to abstain from court appearances.The bars had decided to submit a memorandum to the President, PM, CJI Surya Kant and senior Collegium judges, seeking a permanent full-time CJ for Rajasthan HC and an immediate end to the “targeted file system” across the state.The confrontation followed three letters Justice Sandeep Mehta wrote to the CJI on Aug 2, 10 and 17, seeking Justice Sharma’s transfer out of Rajasthan.Mehta accused Justice Sharma of misusing administrative powers and interfering in case listing, and sought a CJ from another state.In Jaipur, lawyers gathered outside Justice Sharma’s courtroom, shouted slogans and staged a brief sit-in Monday. Addressing an open court after lawyers blocked appearances before his bench, the acting CJ said: “The situation is a little tense today, as the lawyers are not allowing anyone to appear before the court.”Jodhpur bars appealed to lawyers across Rajasthan to join the movement.
Article Summary: Supreme Court Collegium recommended Justice Sanjay K Agarwal of Chhattisgarh HC as Chief Justice of Rajasthan HC. The Collegium also recommended Justice Pushpendra Singh Bhati as CJ of J&K HC. Hours before the recommendation, Sharma decided to abstain from judicial work from Sept 1 to 5.

Article Title: D4vd’s private lawyers withdraw from murder case as public defender takes over his legal representation
Article Text:
D4vd, whose real name is David Anthony Burke, now has a Los Angeles County public defender representing him after his private lawyers withdrew from the case. (Image via: Getty)

Why D4vd’s private lawyers are no longer handling the case

What charges is D4vd facing?

What happens next in the D4vd case?

D4vd, whose real name is David Anthony Burke, now has a different legal team handling the murder case against him. At an August 31, 2026 hearing, his private attorneys were allowed to step away from representing him, and the Los Angeles County Public Defender’s Office was appointed in their place. Burke confirmed the change in court and pleaded not guilty again. The move comes after months of high-profile proceedings surrounding the death of 14-year-old Celeste Abigail Rivas Hernandez. The singer remains in custody without bail while the case moves forward. A judge had already found enough evidence for the charges to proceed after a roughly five-day preliminary hearing in July. His next hearing is scheduled for October 2026. The shift in representation also marks a major change from the earlier stage of the case, when Burke was represented by private attorneys including Blair Berk, Marilyn Bednarski and Regina Peter.The change in counsel happened during the August 31 arraignment or re-arraignment. The court determined that Burke qualified for appointed representation and brought in the Los Angeles County Public Defender’s Office.New counsel includes Walid (Fouad) Kandeel.Burke’s former lawyers said they still support him and indicated that there was no conflict behind the decision. They also said the choice to change representation was Burke’s own. That keeps the focus on the legal change itself rather than suggesting that the former team had suddenly turned against their client.The timing is also notable because the case has already gone through a major evidentiary stage. During the July preliminary hearing, prosecutors presented testimony and evidence covering digital records, forensic findings, purchases and other parts of their case. Judge Charlaine Olmedo found probable cause on all counts and ordered Burke to stand trial.Burke has pleaded not guilty to first-degree murder with special circumstances, continuous sexual abuse of a child under 14, and unlawful mutilation of human remains. Prosecutors allege that he was involved in a sexual relationship with Celeste that began when she was 13, while he was 18.The homicide case centers on prosecutors’ claim that Celeste was killed in April 2025 after threatening to expose the relationship and damage Burke’s career. Her remains were later discovered in the front trunk, or “frunk,” of his Tesla in September 2025.Prosecutors have presented a case built around texts, photographs, location records, Uber data, purchase records, DNA findings and other forensic material. Burke’s defense has rejected the prosecution’s narrative and maintained his innocence.No trial date had been firmly set as of the August 31 hearing. The immediate next step is another court appearance in October, with reports placing that date around October 9 or October 19.The case now moves ahead with the public defender’s office leading Burke’s defense. His legal position has not changed: he has pleaded not guilty and remains in custody without bail while the allegations continue through the court process.
Article Summary: D4vd, whose real name is David Anthony Burke, now has a different legal team handling the murder case against him. At an August 31, 2026 hearing, his private attorneys were allowed to step away from representing him and the Los Angeles County Public Defender’s Office was appointed in their place. The move comes after months of high-profile proceedings surrounding the death of 14-year-old Celeste Abigail Rivas Hernandez.

Article Title: ABVP pulls off a rare repeat in Panjab University polls: Retains president post, 1st back-to-back win since 2014
Article Text:
Chandigarh, Aug 31 (ANI): Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) and SOI (Student Organisation of India) members celebrate after ABVP candidate Ankit Bidhan won the Punjab University Student Council election, in Chandigarh on Monday. (ANI Video Grab)

Retains PUCSC Prez Post, First Back-to-Back Wins Since ’14





CHANDIGARH: After ending its 48-year wait for the PUCSC presidency last year, ABVP retained the post on Monday, becoming the first student organisation since NSUI's back-to-back victories in 2013 and 2014 to achieve consecutive wins. The margin between the two triumphs is strikingly small.ABVP's presidential tally rose by just one vote, from Gaurav Veer Sohal's 3,148 last year to Ankit Bidhan's 3,149 this year. Yet that solitary vote marks the difference between a historic breakthrough and an equally historic repeat.The total presidential vote was almost identical too. Last year, the eight candidates and NOTA together polled 9,613 votes; this year, the four candidates and NOTA accounted for 9,610. The size of the presidential vote pool barely changed- but its distribution did.In 2025, Sohal’s 3,148 votes were followed by Student Front’s Sumit Kumar at 2,660, NSUI’s Parabjot Singh Gill at 1,359 and ASAP’s Mankirat Mann at 1,184. This year, Ankit’s 3,149 was followed by ASAP’s Aadil Brar at 2,637, NSUI’s Gurman Singh Sidhu at 2,263 and SATH’s Darshpreet Singh at 1,387. NOTA fell from 188 to 174.The change in the field matters. Sohal had won 32.75 per cent of the presidential vote last year; Ankit’s share is almost identical at 32.8 per cent.Yet the winning margin increased from 488 to 512 votes. ABVP’s vote base has effectively remained unchanged while its lead has grown.That points to the opposition arithmetic. Last year, Sumit alone came within 488 votes of Sohal, while Gill and Mann together polled 2,543. This year, the opposition vote was still larger collectively, but it was divided among three challengers, with none matching Sumit’s 2,660.For ABVP, there was another significant change. Last year, the organisation itself was divided, with the ABVP Front contesting the vice-president’s post separately; its candidate Naveen Kumar polled 2,828. This year, the outfit went to the polls together.
Article Summary: ABVP becomes the first student organisation since NSUI's back-to-back victories in 2013 and 2014 to achieve consecutive wins. The margin between the two triumphs is strikingly small. ABVP's presidential tally rose by just one vote, from Gaurav Veer Sohal's 3,148 last year to Ankit Bidhan's 3,.149 this year.

Article Title: In 1978, Richard Branson bought a bare 74-acre Caribbean island for $180,000; it now shelters more than 140 animal species, including breeding lemurs and giant tortoises
Article Text:
An aerial view of Necker Island in the British Virgin Islands, a private island in the Caribbean. Credits - Wikimedia Commons

A reluctant purchase becomes a passion

Building a home for species with nowhere else to go

The Great House on Necker Island, built after Hurricane Irene. Credits - Wikipedia

A sanctuary that sustains itself

In 1978, Richard Branson, then 28, paid $180,000 for a small, uninhabited island in the British Virgin Islands. Necker Island had no fresh water source, no buildings and barely any vegetation beyond scrub and cactus. Nearly fifty years after the purchase, and roughly four decades since the resort itself was completed, that same 74-acre island supports a working conservation programme that shelters well over 140 species, several of which now breed there naturally, including lemurs from Madagascar and giant tortoises from the Seychelles.Branson has told the story of the purchase many times over the years, and the details rarely change. According to an account he has given describing the negotiation, he first visited the British Virgin Islands on a trip meant to impress a woman he was pursuing at the time, having been offered a free look at the islands by a realtor who did not realise how little money Branson actually had. The asking price for Necker was around six million dollars, far beyond what he could afford at the time, running an eight-year-old record label, so Branson made an opening offer of just $100,000.The seller turned him down at first but came back a year later, still unable to find a buyer, and eventually accepted a revised offer of $180,000. At that point he owned essentially raw land, with no infrastructure, and the sale came with a condition that he build a resort on the site within four years. Turning that bare ground into something worth visiting took nearly a decade and set the pattern for what followed: a slow, deliberate transformation rather than a quick development.The wildlife did not arrive all at once, and it was introduced deliberately. Over the decades since the resort was completed, Branson and his team have deliberately introduced species that were struggling in their native ranges, choosing Necker specifically because its isolation from the mainland makes it easier to protect animals from predators and disease, even though the island itself operates as a small, tightly controlled private resort where guest access to the animals is limited and managed by the conservation team. As Branson explains in a PBS documentary filmed on the island, lemurs have become one of what he calls the island's flagship conservation species, brought in after habitat loss in Madagascar left many of their relatives fighting for survival at home. Giant tortoises, native to the Aldabra atoll in the Seychelles, followed a similar path, arriving as part of a breeding programme rather than as a decorative addition to the grounds. Flamingos, macaws, iguanas and a rotating cast of other species have joined them, each one added with the specific aim of giving vulnerable animals a secure place to establish new populations. That patient approach appears to be paying off in the way conservationists actually measure success, through births rather than just headcounts.Today, the tortoises in particular have reached a milestone that is rare in captive conservation work, breeding naturally on the island rather than relying on animals shipped in from elsewhere to maintain their numbers. The breeding success became especially significant in 2021, when the island recorded its first Aldabra giant tortoise hatchlings. The young animals were discovered soon after emerging from their nests and were monitored by the island's conservation team to make sure they remained healthy. The event showed that the tortoises were not simply surviving in an introduced population but were completing an important part of their life cycle on Necker itself. The island's wildlife programme has followed a similar approach with other species, creating conditions in which animals can establish themselves rather than simply being displayed for visitors. Virgin Limited Edition now describes Necker as a natural breeding ground for several rare species, including Madagascan lemurs, giant tortoises, rock lizards and flamingos.A dedicated wildlife team now manages the island's animal population full time, treating Necker less like a private garden and more like a functioning sanctuary with its own breeding programmes and veterinary oversight. Branson himself has framed it in exactly those terms in his own public comments, describing a personal commitment to protecting disappearing species that has clearly outlasted his initial reasons for buying the place at all. Necker Island remains one of a small number of personal purchases from that era that developed decades later into an active conservation programme.
Article Summary: Richard Branson bought Necker Island in 1978 for just $180,000. The 74-acre island now supports a working conservation programme. It shelters well over 140 species, including lemurs from Madagascar and giant tortoises from the Seychelles. A dedicated wildlife team manages the island's population full time.

Article Title: Inspiring story on parenthood: “I gave up my childhood to be able to have my children’s childhood” – What Andre Agassi and wife Steffi Graf’s parenting journey teaches about raising a family
Article Text:
Inspiring story on parenthood: “I gave up my childhood to be able to have my children’s childhood” – What Andre Agassi and wife Steffi Graf’s parenting journey teaches about raising a family

What did Andre Agassi mean when he said, “I gave up my childhood to be able to have my children’s childhood”?

How did becoming a father change Agassi’s view of his own childhood?

How did Steffi Graf fit into Agassi’s approach to raising their children?

What does Agassi’s quote tell us about his idea of parenthood?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Andre Agassi’s words, “I gave up my childhood to be able to have my children’s childhood,” offer a deeply personal look at how becoming a parent changed the tennis legend’s view of his own life. Agassi grew up in a world where tennis was not simply a sport but a major part of his everyday life, with intense training and expectations starting at a very young age. Years later, after becoming one of tennis’ biggest stars, he and his wife, fellow tennis legend Steffi Graf, built a family life around their two children, Jaden and Jaz. For Agassi, watching his children grow gave him the chance to experience some of the simple moments of childhood that he felt he had missed himself.The quote is closely connected to Agassi’s own experience growing up. He started playing tennis as a young child and was pushed toward the sport by his father, Mike Agassi. His father had a clear dream for him: he wanted his son to become one of the best tennis players in the world.That dream eventually came true.Agassi went on to become world No. 1 and won eight Grand Slam singles titles during his career. But reaching that level meant spending much of his childhood training, competing and preparing for professional tennis.For a young child, that kind of life can leave little room for ordinary experiences. Instead of having complete freedom to decide how he wanted to spend his time, Agassi’s days were largely connected to tennis.That is where his famous quote becomes especially powerful.When he says he “gave up” his childhood, he is looking back at the years he spent becoming a professional athlete. But he is also talking about what those sacrifices eventually allowed him to do.His success gave him the freedom to step away from tennis and spend more time with his family. It allowed him to be present as his children grew up.In other words, Agassi may have missed parts of his own childhood, but later he had the opportunity to sit beside his children and watch them experience theirs. For him, that became a kind of second chance.Fatherhood gave Andre Agassi a different way of looking at his past. When he watched Jaden and Jaz grow up, he could see the small moments of childhood from a parent’s point of view.He could watch them discover what they liked, make their own choices and develop personalities separate from their famous parents.Those moments were very different from the childhood Agassi had experienced.His early years were strongly connected to the tennis court. His father believed that constant practice and discipline were necessary if Andre Agassi was going to become a champion. That approach helped produce an incredible tennis career, but it also meant that Agassi’s childhood was far from ordinary.As a father, he wanted something different for his children.Instead of seeing childhood as preparation for a future career, Agassi wanted Jaden and Jaz to enjoy the years they were living through.That is one of the most important ideas behind his quote. He was not simply saying that he wanted to give his children more material things or better opportunities. He wanted to give them time.Time to grow.Time to explore.Time to make mistakes.Time to decide what they wanted for themselves.This became especially important because Agassi knew from personal experience how powerful parental expectations can be. He had spent years trying to become the player his father wanted him to be. As a parent, he had the chance to make sure his own children did not feel that same pressure.Steffi Graf’s role in the family’s story is important because she understood Agassi’s world better than almost anyone. Like her husband, Graf was introduced to tennis at a very young age and went on to become one of the greatest players in the history of the sport.Steffi Graf won 22 Grand Slam singles titles and spent years at the top of women’s tennis before retiring in 1999. Agassi and Graf later married and raised their two children, Jaden and Jaz.Together, they had something unusual in common: both parents knew exactly what it took to become a tennis champion, but they also knew the pressure that came with that journey.That understanding appears to have influenced the way they raised their children.Despite having two parents who were global tennis stars, Jaden and Jaz were not simply expected to follow the same path.Jaden developed a passion for baseball rather than choosing tennis as his main sport. Jaz has also been able to follow her own interests. Andre Agassi and Graf have supported their children without making their parents’ careers the center of their lives.That is particularly meaningful when viewed alongside Agassi’s quote.The couple had already achieved what many athletes spend their entire lives chasing. They did not need their children to continue that legacy for them.Instead, they could give their children something that both parents understood the value of: choice.Agassi has also spoken warmly about Graf and the role she plays in his life. Their shared experience in professional sports gave them an understanding of the demands and sacrifices that come with elite competition.For their family, giving their children the freedom to choose their own paths became more important than creating another generation of tennis champions.At its heart, Agassi’s quote is about turning his own difficult experiences into something positive for his children.He cannot go back and change the childhood he had. He cannot erase the years of training, pressure and expectations that came with becoming a tennis player.But he can choose what kind of childhood his own children experience.That is what makes the quote about much more than tennis.Many parents work hard because they want their children to have opportunities they did not have themselves. Agassi’s story takes that idea one step further. His goal was not simply to provide his children with a comfortable life. He wanted to be present for the experiences that make childhood special.His words also show that parenthood can change the way people understand their own past.The same childhood that once felt difficult to Agassi became part of what helped him understand his children better. His experiences taught him what pressure can feel like, which may have made him more aware of the importance of giving his own children freedom.And Steffi Graf was there beside him, bringing her own experience as a former champion and a parent.Together, Agassi and Graf chose not to make their children’s lives about living up to their parents’ names. They allowed Jaden and Jaz to build identities of their own.That may be the most powerful part of Agassi’s words.He spent his childhood becoming a tennis champion. But when he became a father, he did not want his children to spend their childhood becoming something for him.He wanted to watch them simply be children.So, when Agassi says, “I gave up my childhood to be able to have my children’s childhood,” he is not only talking about sacrifice. He is talking about perspective, presence and love.He gave years of his life to tennis. Those years helped him become a champion and eventually gave him the freedom to step back and focus on his family.For Agassi, one of the greatest rewards was not another trophy or achievement. It was being able to watch his children grow up on their own terms, with Graf by his side.That is what makes his quote so relatable. Parenthood does not allow us to rewrite our own childhoods, but it can give us the chance to create a different childhood for the next generation.
Article Summary: Tennis legend Andre Agassi and wife Steffi Graf have two children, Jaden and Jaz. Agassi’s famous quote, “I gave up my childhood to be able to have my children's childhood,” offers a look at how becoming a parent changed his view of his own life. For Agassi, watching his children grow gave him the chance to experience some of the simple moments of childhood.

Article Title: Alaska used rotenone to eliminate invasive pike from an entire lake; the pike vanished, and 6,836 Arctic char were later stocked to rebuild the native fishery
Article Text:
Representative image

Why northern pike are a problem in Alaska

Rotenone: a targeted, temporary reset

Alaska eliminates invasive pike and restocks lake with 6,836 Arctic char

Stormy Lake: a case study in eradication and recovery

Other lakes, similar stories

Why Arctic char matter

Balancing restoration with public concern

A tool, not a silver bullet

In a remote corner of Southcentral Alaska, state biologists carried out a dramatic restoration: they treated an entire lake with rotenone, a plant-derived piscicide, to wipe out an invasive population of northern pike. After the treatment, post-surveys confirmed the pike were gone. The next step was rebuilding what had been lost. In June 2013, the Alaska Department of Fish and Game (ADF&G) stocked 6,836 hatchery-reared Arctic char fingerlings into the now pike-free lake, jump-starting the recovery of a native fishery that had been pushed out by the predator. This account draws on ADF&G’s technical reports and project summaries documenting the rotenone treatment and restocking. Read on to know more:Northern pike are not native to most of Southcentral Alaska. They were illegally introduced into several lakes in the mid-20th century and have since spread through connected waterways, especially as warming temperatures and changing hydrology make it easier for them to move and survive. As apex predators, pike eat large quantities of native fish, including salmon, trout, grayling and char. In some lakes, they have all but replaced native sport fish, collapsing local angling opportunities and altering food webs.ADF&G describes pike as a major threat to endemic fish populations and has pursued a mix of suppression and eradication strategies depending on the waterbody. In isolated lakes where pike can be completely removed, the agency has turned to rotenone as the most practical and efficient tool.Rotenone is a naturally occurring compound derived from certain tropical plants. It has been used for decades in fisheries management to remove unwanted fish from lakes and streams. When applied at carefully calculated concentrations, it blocks oxygen uptake in fish gills, killing fish while leaving most other aquatic organisms unaffected. The chemical breaks down relatively quickly in sunlight and warm water; in many Alaskan projects, detectable levels drop to near zero within weeks to months.There are only two proven methods to eradicate invasive fish from lakes: completely draining the waterbody or using a piscicide like rotenone. For most lakes, draining is not feasible, making rotenone the default option for full eradication. Before treatment, ADF&G typically relocates any desirable native fish, such as salmon or trout, to safe holding areas or other lakes, then treats the target lake and its outlet streams to ensure no pike survive.Stormy Lake, near Anchorage, is one of the clearest examples of this approach. In fall 2012, ADF&G treated Stormy Lake and its outlet creek with liquid rotenone to eradicate an established northern pike population. Post-treatment evaluations—including netting and electrofishing surveys, found no surviving pike, confirming the treatment’s success.Once the rotenone had fully degraded (by late January 2013, about four months after application), the agency began restocking. Native fish that had been held in offsite net pens were reintroduced in March 2013, and on June 17, 2013, ADF&G stocked 6,836 hatchery-reared Arctic char fingerlings into Stormy Lake. These char were of mixed Stormy Lake and Dolly Varden Lake parentage, helping to re-establish a robust, genetically diverse population.The project’s final report, published in ADF&G’s Sport Fish Research series, describes the effort as a successful model for eradicating invasive pike and restoring native fisheries.Stormy Lake is not unique. ADF&G has used rotenone to remove pike from multiple lakes in the Anchorage and Mat-Su areas, including Sand Lake, Anderson Lake and Kings Lake. In each case, the sequence is similar: treat the lake, confirm pike are gone, then restock with native species such as rainbow trout, Arctic char and grayling.For example, after rotenone treatments in 2020, Anderson and Kings lakes were declared pike-free and added to the Northern Cook Inlet stocking program in 2021. Both lakes were restocked with rainbow trout, restoring sport fisheries that had been lost to pike predation. In Anchorage, pike have been eradicated from all but one of five lakes where they were confirmed, with Lower Fire Lake remaining a management challenge.Arctic char are a prized native species in Alaska, valued both ecologically and by anglers. They thrive in cold, clear lakes and are an important part of the natural food web. In lakes where pike have been removed, char are often a key restocking target because they can grow to good size, support recreational fishing and help re-establish a more natural predator–prey balance.In Stormy Lake, the 6,836 char stocked in 2013 were intended to re-create a self-sustaining population that could eventually support a catch-and-release or limited-harvest fishery. Monitoring in subsequent years showed that char, along with other restocked natives, were surviving and growing, indicating the lake was returning to a healthier, pre-pike state.The use of rotenone is not without controversy. Killing all fish in a lake, even temporarily, can be unsettling for nearby residents and anglers. ADF&G addresses these concerns through public meetings, environmental assessments and detailed explanations of why the treatment is necessary and how risks are managed.Agency biologists emphasise that the alternative, allowing pike to remain, is often worse for native biodiversity and long-term fishing opportunities. In lakes where pike have taken hold, native species may never recover without a full reset. Rotenone, used correctly, offers a way to hit that reset button and then rebuild the fishery with native species.While rotenone has proven effective in isolated lakes, it is not a solution for every pike-infested waterbody. In large, connected systems like much of the Mat-Su Valley, complete eradication is currently impossible because pike can simply move back in from untreated areas. There, ADF&G focuses on suppression, using gillnets, targeted rotenone applications in key tributaries, and liberal harvest rules to keep pike numbers down in priority fisheries.Projects like Stormy Lake show where eradication is still feasible: in relatively closed basins where pike can be fully removed and native fish reintroduced. For those lakes, the combination of rotenone treatment and strategic stocking—like the 6,836 Arctic char released in 2013, offers a path back to a more natural, resilient fishery. For Alaska’s fisheries managers, such projects demonstrate that invasive predators can sometimes be removed and native fish populations rebuilt when the conditions are right. Article Summary: Northern pike are not native to most of Southcentral Alaska. They were illegally introduced into several lakes in the mid-20th century. Pike eat large quantities of native fish, including salmon, trout, grayling and char. They have all but replaced native sport fish, collapsing local angling opportunities.

Article Title: “Three-against-one situation”: El Rubius opens up on being “targeted” in MrBeast’s viral $1M challenge
Article Text:
El Rubius reacted honestly after his elimination from MrBeast’s $1 million challenge, calling it “unfair” and claiming he was targeted in a three-against-one situation. Despite his frustration, he thanked fans and gave away his $50,000 winnings. His response felt real and balanced, especially after MrBeast’s team later sent him a cake, softening the moment.

El Rubius reflects on a tough and “unfair” exit







El Rubius did not just walk away from MrBeast’s $1 million streamer challenge. He opened up. Soon after his elimination, the Spanish creator shared a raw reaction with fans, giving them a closer look at what the experience felt like from inside the game. It was not polished or carefully framed. It felt real, and that is exactly why it caught attention so quickly.The clip and his response have since fueled conversations across the streaming space. Some viewers believe intense competitions like this naturally lead to uneven situations. Others feel Rubius may have had a point about being singled out. Either way, his words have added a human layer to a challenge that many only saw as entertainment.Speaking through an Instagram Story, Rubius did not hide his frustration, but he also made sure to thank his supporters. He said, "Guys, I just got knocked out of the game. It was a bit of an unfair elimination, but hey, at least I managed to walk away with $50,000 for you all, which I’ve already distributed. It went to the mods, the subs, and the non-subs alike."He further added, "I’m happy, of course, though admittedly, it was incredibly tough.I wasn't really a fan of the challenge itself, either. But then again... it was basically a three-against-one situation the entire time. I mean, they were targeting me specifically the whole way through. I kept trying to go after RaKai, but, well, he actually just got eliminated in the end. So, at least justice was served for Abraham. Abraham, if you’re watching this, we were all rooting for you, and standing right there with you."His message carried mixed emotions. There was disappointment, yes, but also pride in how he handled things. Giving away his $50,000 winnings to his community stood out as a gesture that meant more than the result itself.He continued with another honest note, saying, "And in the end, karma finally caught up with that little punk. Sorry, I’m being a bit toxic right now, but let's just hope the MrBeast team doesn't see this! Guys, thank you all so much. Seriously, thank you for all the support and for just being there."He added, "Every time I asked for something in the chat or whatever it was, you guys were right there. You’re incredible. I’m a little disappointed in myself, personally, mostly for not performing better, but hey, I gave it my all, and we still walked away with $50,000, so we’ve got to look on the bright side. All right, guys, big hugs to all my brothers out there!"Interestingly, the story did not end with frustration. Later that day, Rubius revealed that MrBeast’s team had sent him a cake after his exit. It was a small gesture, but it shifted the mood. It showed that even in a high-pressure challenge, there is still room for respect.In the end, Rubius’ reaction felt honest and grounded. That is what stayed with people.
Article Summary: El Rubius was eliminated from MrBeast's $1 million streamer challenge. He called it "unfair" and said he was targeted in a three-against-one situation. Despite his frustration, he thanked fans and gave away his $50,000 winnings.

Article Title: IPL craze costs techie Rs 1.46 lakh in fake RCB vs CSK ticket scam
Article Text:
Image credit: AI generated pic

RCB register their second win

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you think the demand for IPL tickets is too high every season? Yes, it's excessive. No, it's just right. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: IPL comes and the demand for tickets and passes go soaring up by the fans. The desperation to get inside the stadium to watch their favourite teams in action in the IPL go high and high. When the tickets get sold out, the demand gets too hig, and the cricket fans even ask for tickets in black. But for a 25-year-old techie the craze for IPL tickets for RCB vs CSK turned too costly and he was duped for a massive Rs. 1.46 lakh.The techie, a resident of B Narayanapura, fell into a trap by a post posted by a fraudster who posed himself as a ticket seller on Instagram.As per a report in Deccan Herald, the techie alleged in a complaint to Mahadevapura Police that an individual claiming to be Sumit Biswal promised he could arrange IPL tickets along with food coupons.As per the techie, Biswal was introduced him as a senior supervisor for ticket counter at M Chinnaswamy Stadium"He asked me to come near the stadium gate number 10, saying someone would deliver the tickets within minutes, and even sent an email confirmation to gain my trust," the complainant told Deccan Herald."Initially, I agreed to buy two tickets for Rs 3,700 each,but he kept asking for more money under various pretexts such as refundable security deposits, additional ID cards and food coupons.Trusting him, I made multiple payments - even using my mother’s bank account after exhausting my own limits—and ended up transferring around Rs 1.46 lakh," he added.Bhuvneshwar Kumar’s incisive spell of 3-41, coming after a marauding batting show from Tim David, Rajat Patidar and Devdutt Padikkal, propelled Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) to a commanding 43-run victory over Chennai Super Kings (CSK) in their IPL 2026 encounter at the M Chinnaswamy Stadium on Sunday.The contest saw RCB’s batting unit dismantle CSK’s attack with relentless hitting, as David’s 70 not out off just 25 balls and Patidar’s unbeaten 48 off only 19 balls provided for the late fireworks after Padikkal’s fluent 50 off 29 balls had set the tone for the daunting total.Their combined effort lifted RCB to a daunting 250/3, thus setting a new record for highest total in IPL 2026. In reply, CSK faltered under scoreboard pressure, with Sarfaraz Khan’s 50 off 24 balls and Prashant Veer’s 43 the lone acts of resistance amid a string of failures from the top order.Bhuvneshwar was at his disciplined best and even crossed the 200-mark in terms of wickets in IPL, with others also chipping in as CSK were bowled out for 207 in 19.4 overs. The comprehensive win also meant RCB have registered four consecutive triumphs over CSK for the first time in the IPL’s history.
Article Summary: Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) beat Chennai Super Kings (CSK) in IPL 2026 encounter at the M Chinnaswamy Stadium on Sunday. Tim David, Rajat Patidar and Devdutt Padikkal put on a marauding batting show to lift RCB to a daunting 250/3. RCB have registered four consecutive triumphs over CSK for the first time in the IPL’s history.

Article Title: Clavicular Viral Controversy: "Trans women are.....": Clavicular’s viral moment with trans women sparks fresh conversation on internet culture
Article Text:
A viral clip featuring Clavicular and trans women is gaining attention for its calm and honest tone. The conversation explores how online language and trends move across communities. Instead of conflict, the exchange highlights shared influence and mutual awareness. Viewers are engaging with its thoughtful nature, as it reflects how internet culture evolves through collaboration rather than ownership.

Clavicular and trans women share a surprising realization about online trends







The video of Clavicular, a short-video producer, is going around the Internet, yet not the reason why. There is no yelling or over-the-top drama. It is a mere, everyday talk that seems almost novel nowadays, in the age of internet, which is overflowing with content. The scene is easy-going, the tone of the narrative is straightforward, and the characters appear more concerned with conversation than combat.The message that is being addressed is the flow of the conversation. It discusses internet culture, the way people communicate with one another and the place of trends. Rather than bringing out a debate, the encounter towards curiosity. It quietly brings attention to something that a lot of people who use the internet notice but don't often say out loud. People in different communities often have a bigger impact on each other than they think.The conversation begins with a confident and lighthearted comment from one of the trans women present. She says, "You know that trans women are like the OG lip masters, right? We are very talented in the program. Like, I do the peptides, I'm on Zeta." Her tone carries a mix of pride and humor, setting a relaxed vibe at the table.Clavicular responds in a way that keeps the mood steady but adds a different angle.He says, "That is funny because you guys were using a lot of the words in like the South Korean subreddits in like 2014." It’s not confrontational. If anything, it feels like an observation. He points to how certain words and ideas may have traveled across different online spaces over time.Another voice joins in and brings the moment full circle. "Guys, we're like the OGs. I saw a couple of posts about that. We're like copying each other." That line hits in a simple but honest way. It reflects something familiar. Online culture is rarely created in isolation. It grows through sharing, borrowing, and sometimes even unknowingly repeating.That's what makes the clip so powerful. It doesn't want to make a point or win an argument. It only shows a group of people talking, listening, and figuring something out together.This moment feels different in a space where viral content often leads to fights. It reminds people that conversations can be calm, thoughtful, and still important. And sometimes, that honest silence is what makes it work.
Article Summary: A viral clip featuring Clavicular and trans women is gaining attention for its calm and honest tone. The conversation explores how online language and trends move across communities. Viewers are engaging with its thoughtful nature, as it reflects how internet culture evolves through collaboration.

Article Title: ‘This is the reason they are in the mess’: Ex-Pakistan coach tears into Mohsin Naqvi-led PCB
Article Text:
Pakistan's Mohammad Abbas celebrates with teammates ( Reuters)

Mickey Arthur post

Seven Pakistan players sent home

Arthur questions PCB’s constant changes

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Former Pakistan head coach Mickey Arthur has criticised the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) for making sweeping changes to the squad and coaching staff. His comments follow the team’s disastrous defeat at Lord’s, which left them trailing 2-0 in the three-match series against England.The PCB confirmed on Monday that seven players would be sent home after Pakistan suffered their second consecutive heavy defeat, losing the Lord’s Test by 194 runs. The decision also affects the coaching setup, with Test coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and bowling coach Umar Gul being asked to leave England.White-ball coach Mike Hesson will now oversee Pakistan for the third and final Test in Birmingham.Arthur, who has previously coached the Pakistan men’s team, questioned the PCB’s approach and accused the board of repeatedly making changes without allowing the team to develop stability.“Absolutely ridiculous decisions by the PCB-this is the reason they are in the mess they are, because they constantly chop and change players, coaches and selectors, and there is no stability! Planning, stability and structure =Consistent performance,” Arthur wrote on X (formerly Twitter).The PCB’s decision came after Pakistan failed to make either of the first two Tests competitive.Pakistan were beaten by an innings and 103 runs in the opening Test before England completed another convincing victory at Lord’s, winning by 194 runs.Following the latest defeat, the PCB announced that Mohammad Rizwan, Imam-ul-Haq, Salman Ali Agha, Ali Usman, Aamir Jamal, Muhammad Awais Zafar and Khurram Shahzad would return home.Seven replacements have been named, with the incoming group consisting of five players yet to make their Test debuts and two who have already represented Pakistan in the format.Among the replacements are Saim Ayub and Abdullah Fazal, who have played eight and two Tests respectively. Left-arm spin-bowling all-rounder Arafat Minhas has also been added after representing Pakistan in three ODIs and four T20Is.Pakistan’s poor performances have intensified scrutiny on the team and its administration. The side have failed to reach the fifth day in either Test, while their batting has repeatedly collapsed under pressure.Arthur argued that the latest changes risk creating even more instability within a team already struggling for consistency.The former coach believes Pakistan’s problems cannot be solved simply by repeatedly changing players, coaches and selectors, stressing the importance of long-term planning and structure.The latest overhaul also means Hesson will have to quickly adapt to the Test environment before the final match of the series.Pakistan’s difficult tour has left them at the bottom of the World Test Championship standings, with one Test still remaining against England.
Article Summary: Former Pakistan head coach Mickey Arthur has criticised the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) for making sweeping changes to the squad and coaching staff. His comments follow the team's disastrous defeat at Lord’s, which left them trailing 2-0 in the three-match series against England. The PCB confirmed on Monday that seven players would be sent home after Pakistan suffered their second consecutive heavy defeat.
